rows.description: A stranger in the game asks if I am okay after I lose badly. It feels nice, but kindness online still needs care; I stay friendly and never share private information.

rows.description: A person messages me and seems interesting, and I want to reply. Curiosity is natural, but I check with a parent before chatting, and I never share my school, address or photos.

rows.description: A stranger says I am so mature and special and asks me to keep our chats secret. Flattery plus secrecy is a red flag. I stop replying and tell a parent or teacher, and I have done nothing wrong.

rows.description: A stranger says he knows where I live and I freeze. It is right to be scared. I save the messages, do not answer and immediately tell a trusted adult; help is available.

rows.description: I chatted with someone I should not have and I am afraid to tell my parents. Shame keeps children silent; telling them early is the bravest and safest step, and they are on my side.

rows.description: My friend is secretly chatting with a stranger who asks for photos. Being loyal means telling a trusted adult, even if she gets angry, because her safety matters more than the secret.

rows.description: A classmate posts a mean message about me in a group chat. I feel hurt and exposed. I can save the proof, avoid replying in anger and tell a parent or teacher; it is not my fault.

rows.description: I ask an AI assistant many questions and love how it answers instantly. It helps me learn, and I can also double-check with books and teachers because it can be wrong.

rows.description: I ask the AI to do my homework and feel relieved. But if it does my thinking, I learn nothing and cannot answer in class. I can use it to explain things, then try the work myself.

rows.description: I believe everything the AI says because it sounds confident. A wise child learns that fluent answers can still be mistaken, and checks important facts.
